The fitting results after run_2 show M5 as the best, but many mechanisms are within a narrow NLL range, indicating continued ambiguity. The aim now is to propose a new experiment that avoids product and instead varies another key parameter—substrate concentration—to stress different aspects of the mechanisms.

<hypothesis>
We have explored the effect of catalyst concentration at high substrate. Now we probe the effect of substrate concentration by reducing it to a level comparable to the catalyst. Using S=0.2 M and cat=0.01 M (20:1 ratio) contrasts with run_1 (100:1) and run_2 (10:1). At lower substrate, mechanisms that involve substrate saturation or substrate-dependent steps (e.g., M7 with S+catS<=>catS2, M11 with S+cat=>inactive_catS, M16 with S+catS=>inactive_catS2) may show distinct kinetic signatures. Additionally, mechanisms with dimerization (M2, M3) or bimolecular deactivation (M13, M18, M19) could behave differently when substrate is not in large excess. This condition avoids extreme regimes (e.g., very high or very low catalyst) and should yield well-behaved data for fitting. By comparing the time courses at high and low substrate, we can discriminate mechanisms based on their functional dependence on substrate concentration.
</hypothesis>
